true_answer: Cultures may deﬁne other units of time, such as the week, for the purpose of scheduling regular activities that do not easily coincide with months or years. Many cultures use diﬀerent baselines for their calendars' starting years. Historically, several countries have based their calendars on regnal years, a calendar based on the reign of their current sovereign. For example, the year 2006 in Japan is year 18 Heisei, with Heisei being the era name of Emperor Akihito.
